short: A Scottish king of seventeen years, remembered through a play he would not recognise.
full:
Macbeth was mormaer of Moray and the grandson of a king when he killed Duncan I in battle near Elgin in August 1040 and took the throne. Duncan had been young and unsuccessful in war, and the Scottish succession did not yet run strictly from father to son, so the killing was a conventional route to power rather than the crime the play describes.

His reign lasted seventeen years and was secure enough that he left Scotland in 1050 to make a pilgrimage to Rome, where a chronicler records him scattering money to the poor. Duncan's son Malcolm, backed by Earl Siward of Northumbria, invaded in 1054 and again later; Macbeth was killed at Lumphanan in Aberdeenshire in August 1057. His stepson Lulach ruled for a few months before Malcolm III took the throne. Shakespeare's version, written for a Stuart king, follows Holinshed's chronicle rather than the record.
